headline: Newsletter cadence drops from daily to twice weekly at issue 100
detail: Mondays and Wednesdays, in response to a reader survey asking for fewer emails.
quote: With that in mind, from today you’ll receive an update twice a week on Mondays and Wednesdays.
notes: The first cadence change in the series. It thins again to weekly on 12 October 2020 and to roughly monthly through 2022, so the frequency of the newsletters is itself a record of how urgent the situation felt.

headline: UCL reports shutting over 200 buildings and delivering 647 online exams
detail: A hundred-working-day retrospective, also recording 147 student interns appointed to move teaching materials online.
quote: Colleagues from every Faculty, Vice Provost’s Office and Professional Services department have, at speed, first shut down over 200 buildings on campus
notes: UCL's own summary of the first phase, and the source of the 647 online exams figure. Both numbers are UCL's own and are not independently checkable from the archive.

headline: Staff quarantining after non-essential travel must use leave, not paid absence
detail: Prompted by the Foreign Office revoking Spain's travel corridor at short notice on 27 July, and Luxembourg soon after.
quote: From 3 August, where travel is not for agreed essential UCL work, the default position is for the member of staff to work remotely during their period of self-isolation if possible, by agreement with your line manager. If that is not possible, you should take any remaining annual leave entitlement followed by unpaid leave.
notes: A tightening. In June, staff caught by quarantine were offered paid leave as a fallback; from August the fallback is unpaid.

headline: No Detriment Principle for Staff published, covering promotions and appraisals
detail: UCL estimated around 40% of employees had been caring for children or loved ones during the pandemic.
quote: UCL leadership have therefore set out clearly how we are going to ensure that all this is taken into account in our No Detriment Principle for Staff .
notes: The staff counterpart to the student no-detriment principle adopted on 7 April 2020, four months earlier.

headline: UCL undertakes not to reuse teaching recordings without the originator's consent
detail: Setting aside the position in the Intellectual Property Policy, which assigns film and sound recordings to UCL, for the 2019-20 and 2020-21 academic years.
quote: UCL has committed, notwithstanding the position in the UCL Intellectual Property Policy, not to use teaching-related film and sound recordings created during academic years 2019/20 and 2020/21 without the originators’ consent
notes: A staff concern created directly by the move online: recording lectures turned teaching into an asset the policy already claimed.

headline: Face covering policy widened to inside offices, labs and teaching spaces
detail: Strongly encouraged throughout campus and mandatory within two metres of another person, with clear-panel coverings procured centrally for classroom teaching.
quote: Face coverings are now strongly encouraged when you’re on campus, both inside buildings and when moving around campus. This includes in offices, labs and teaching spaces.
notes: The third tightening in two months: 22 May when distancing was impossible, 10 July mandatory when moving around, 12 August extended indoors throughout.

headline: Protecting Time for Work recommendations issued in response to workload data
detail: Meetings in core hours, hour-long meetings cut to 50 minutes, and email and meeting efficiency measures.
quote: Our weekly Your Wellbeing survey continues to highlight that many of you are struggling with your workloads.
notes: A second traceable line from the weekly survey to a policy change, after the cycle racks in July.

headline: UCL accepts all students meeting their original offer after the A level U-turn
detail: Following the government's decision to use teacher-predicted grades rather than the Ofqual algorithm.
quote: We are delighted to accept all students who meet the terms of their original offer.
notes: The decision that produced the exceptionally large first-year intake, which UCL names on 26 August as one cause of the study-space shortage. It is therefore upstream of how crowded campus was in autumn 2020.

headline: All Term One core teaching to be online, with 1 to 2 hours a week face to face
detail: Students free to study on campus or from anywhere in the world, and to change their mind mid-term without penalty.
quote: We’re currently anticipating a maximum of 1-2 hours a week of face to face teaching time, although this will vary depending on programme.
notes: The most concrete statement of how much on-campus contact autumn 2020 actually involved, and essential context for reading the on-campus case counts that begin in October.

headline: Visitors to campus must declare symptoms and register where they went
detail: Contact details and areas visited collected so UCL could respond to cases.
quote: They will also be asked to supply their contact details and the areas of campus they are visiting. We will use this information to make sure campus is as safe as possible and respond to any potential cases of COVID-19 should they occur.
notes: UCL building its own contact-tracing capability three weeks before the case reporting tool was announced.

headline: Staff offices released to students as study space after distancing cuts capacity
detail: Floors in Bidborough House and Torrington Place given over to students, against the 6,000 study spaces available the previous year.
quote: Social distancing put in place to ensure the safety of everyone on campus means that the number of student study spaces on campus will be much reduced compared with the 6,000 we had last year.
notes: Names three compounding causes: distancing, growth in postgraduate applications, and the large first-year intake following the A level U-turn. A direct consequence of the 2 metre decision of 8 July.

headline: Zoom licensed for a year because it was the most reliable platform for China
detail: Supported by ISD from 2 September alongside Blackboard Collaborate and Microsoft Teams.
quote: UCL has purchased a 12-month licence for Zoom, as it is currently the most reliable platform for access from China.
notes: A platform decision driven by where students physically were. Many were expected to study the whole of Term 1 from outside the UK.

headline: All campus buildings open on schedule for the new academic year
detail: Over 100 buildings requiring safety and statutory checks, completed to the July roadmap.
quote: With thanks to the Estates Operations team and colleagues across UCL, all buildings on campus are now open, on schedule and in time for the start of the new term.
notes: Five and a half months after the closure of 20 March 2020. Open, but under the 25% occupancy cap and 2 metre distancing.

headline: Pre-enrolment data used to forecast how many students would be on campus
quote: It is particularly urgent this year, as we will use this to forecast student numbers on campus and manage activities within our 2-metre social distancing guidelines.
notes: UCL predicting campus occupancy from enrolment before it could measure it. The case statistics that began six weeks later gave it a measurement instead.

headline: Student Support Fund opened for students facing severe financial hardship
detail: Prioritising students from low-income families and BAME backgrounds, disabled students and those with experience of care or homelessness, and receiving the Provost's donated salary.
quote: We know that many students are experiencing severe financial hardship this year. The situation for some is so critical that they are being forced to consider leaving UCL.
notes: The destination of the 20% salary reduction announced on 24 April, now opened to staff donations.

headline: Student Success Advisers appointed, one for every 200 undergraduates
detail: Embedded in academic departments and contacting students before and after arrival.
quote: Each Adviser will be responsible for around 200 students, acting as their first point of contact for any questions or problems they may have, and proactively contacting them before and after they arrive.

headline: UCL announces a reporting tool to monitor and respond to cases at UCL
detail: Due mid-September, designed with UCL public health experts who had been advising the government.
quote: This guidance will remain in place until mid-September, when we will launch a new reporting tool to monitor and respond to coronavirus cases at UCL. This system is being designed with UCL public health experts who have been advising the Government.
notes: The origin of the dataset this archive preserves. The published case page first appears in the archive on 12 October 2020, about a month after this announcement, and the first published figure is dated 2020-10-09. This row is the single most important link between the newsletter track and the data track.

headline: Provost notes the national daily case count clearly rising again
detail: Written the week the rule of six was introduced and three weeks before term began.
quote: with the daily national number of new cases clearly on the rise again, it remains a time of great uncertainty
notes: UCL watching national figures because it had none of its own. The reporting tool announced in the same issue is the answer to exactly this.

headline: Rule of six noted as UCL considers its response
quote: the Government has reported a rise in coronavirus cases and limited social gatherings to six people from Monday. UCL is monitoring the situation and considering our response.
notes: Filed on 14 September, the Monday the national limit took effect; reported by UCL on 9 September. A rare case of UCL saying openly that it had not yet decided what to do.

headline: No national pay uplift for 2020-21; UCL raises London weighting by 2%
detail: National negotiations agreed no uplift because of the sector's financial position. UCL kept automatic incremental progression on grades 1 to 9 and backdated the London weighting rise to 1 August.
quote: UCL, like most universities in the UK, takes part in national pay negotiations where it was agreed there would be no pay uplift for 2020–21, due to the financial impact of COVID-19 on the sector nationally.
notes: A sector-level decision by UCEA that UCL partly offset locally. The UCEA settlement is a stage 2 retrieval target for the sector track.

headline: Quality assurance processes temporarily relaxed to cut administrative workload
detail: Internal Quality Review deferred a year for most departments, extenuating circumstances reporting suspended, the emergency module amendment procedure continued, and peer observation reporting suspended.
quote: A series of temporary modifications to quality assurance processes at departmental level has been agreed for 2020-21, to uphold UCL’s academic standards while reducing administrative workload.

headline: Term 1 begins on 28 September, coinciding with Yom Kippur
detail: Departments asked to be flexible about start-of-term requirements for Jewish students observing the fast.
quote: Yom Kippur this year coincides with the first day of term on Monday 28 September, and we would like to encourage all departments to be flexible about start of term requirements and activities
notes: Establishes the first day of Term 1 as 28 September 2020, which is the reference point for reading the October case surge. The published case series begins eleven days later.
